summary_rationale: McKesson Corporation operates the largest pharmaceutical distribution toll-road in North America, generating $403.43 billion in FY2026 GAAP revenue and $5.41 billion in Free Cash Flow within an entrenched three-player oligopoly (McKesson, Cencora, Cardinal Health) controlling over 90% of U.S. drug distribution. Its strategic pivot out of lower-margin European retail, the ongoing separation of Medical-Surgical Solutions (Wellverse, backed by a $1.25 billion Apollo minority stake and $3.23 billion of ring-fenced Med-Surg term loans), and aggressive expansion into higher-margin Oncology & Multispecialty (2.96% adjusted operating margin, up 53% YoY in FY2026) and Prescription Technology Solutions (19.45% adjusted operating margin) structurally elevate consolidated profit pools and capital efficiency. KPI health is PASS_WITH_WATCH rather than an unqualified PASS due to dual-sided concentration (CVS Health at ~24% of FY2026 revenue, though extended through June 2032; top 3 customers at ~45% and top 10 at ~73%; top 10 suppliers at ~71% of purchases), $5.16 billion in remaining opioid litigation liabilities ($600M current + $4.56B long-term as of Sep 30, 2026), $9.21 billion total financial debt, $2.56 billion redeemable noncontrolling interests tied to physician MSOs and Apollo's stake, and emerging policy/cybersecurity risks (IRA Part B, 340B rebate model, and federal class-action lawsuits following the August 2026 data exfiltration incident).
